title: DOE Announces New Genesis Mission Awards to Accelerate Scientific Capability
source_used: The Quantum Insider (carrying the Department of Energy press release); Nextgov/FCW for context
key_facts: The US Department of Energy announced 12 Phase II project awards for the Genesis Mission, totalling $159 million.
The awards aim to use AI, advanced computing and the national laboratories to speed up scientific discovery.
The new selections bring the Phase II total to 14, alongside earlier awards for GridFM 2.0 and Prometheus.
Six new Phase I awards are also being issued.
DOE Under Secretary for Science Darío Gil said the awards let teams take their work to the next level.
Nextgov/FCW adds that DOE also announced $96 million for early-career researchers and a new graduate fellowship.
quote_evidence: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced 12 Phase II project awards for President Trump’s historic Genesis Mission, totaling $159 million, that will expand efforts to harness artificial intelligence (AI), advanced computing, and the nation’s world-class scientific capabilities to accelerate the pace of discovery.
Additionally, six new Phase I awards are being issued, supplementing the earlier round of selections.
why_it_matters_hint: Public money is moving into specific AI-for-science projects at national labs and universities.
